# Spatial redeployment of supplementary income generated by positive externalities associated with local public goods

This dissertation aim to formulate a formula for the spatial redistribution of the supplementary income and to show how its application promotes spatial justice. In order to do this, two models were developed: one for impact evaluation, and the other for estimating supplementary income. Both models made it possible to establish variations of land and property prices (LnPP) associated to new or improved LPGs and to determine their impact zones. As LPGs under evaluation, it was established the bus rapid transit (BRT) system that runs parallel to avenue to Calle 26, Carrera Decima, Calle 80, av. NQS, av. Suba and av. Autonorte, all of them raised transit, Colombia. The spatial redistribution of supplemental income income to be collected through the application of the GDP is determined by the application of the GDP taxes (that is, that it is looking to correct a negative or positive externality mechanism).The proposed process of stability to the secondary level of the economy.The application of this economy to the secondary level of the economy is determined by the economic situation of the economy.The objective of this research is to formulate a spatial redistribution of supplementary income and to show how its application promotes spatial justice.For this purpose two models (impact assessment and alternative income estimation) were developed to establish the variation of the local level, the local level and the local level. This mechanism establishes the neighborhood as a spatial unit of intervention and integrates processes of incident participation to allocate resources to finance new or improved PLPs in low-income urban peripheries. The application of this process of spatial redistribution of suppletory income contributes to spatial justice insofar as this process generates economic landscapes where inequalities decrease
